To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
COX-1 may lose functionality during aging in rats.

the participation of prostanoid in the contractile responses of the thoracic/ab-dominal aorta of prepubescent rats is higher, while in the coronary artery of prepubes- cent rats is lower, when compared with older rats.
the participation of prostanoid in the contractile effects of phenylephine is different in different vascular regions and in pre-pubescente, young and adult rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the participation of the COX-1/COX-2 system in the contractile effects of the phenylephrine and in the vascular response to this agonist during aging.
the role of prostanoids and their receptors in the contractile effects of phenylephrune in the abdominal aortas of young, old and pre-pubescent animals.
the participation of COX- in the contractile responses of thoracic and abdominal aorta and the left coronary artery during aging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the participation of COX- in the contractile responses of the thoracic/ab-dominal aorta and coronary artery during aging is not the same in all tissues and that it is not always associated with changes in the expression levels of COX- and COX-

there are age-dependent differences in the contractile effects of phenylephrime on aorta and coronary arteries of rats, and that the participation of COX- 1 and COX -2 in this contractile response is different in the three age groups.
there is no clear evidence that COX-1 or COX-2 is involved in the contractile effects of phenylephine in the aorta or coronary artery of rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
COX-2 is not a good target for anti-atherogenic drugs.

the contractile response in the aorta of pre-pubescent and adult rats is dependent on the participation of prostanoid receptors and the expression of COs, whereas this participation is not as important in the coronary artery of pre-pubescente and adult rats.
the vascular reactivity of rats can be influenced by animal age and vascular region, and that this reactivity can be modulated by the participation of COX- 1 and COX 2.
The main takeaway from our work is that

COX-1 may have an important role in prostanoids production in the thoracic/abdoimal aorta and the coronaric artery of rats, and that COX-2 has an important role in these arteries of prepubescent rats.

the participation of prostanoid receptors in vascular reactivity changes in rats during aging, and the participation of COX- 1 and COX -2 in the contractility of the aorta is greater in pre-pubescente than in old rats.
the vascular reactivity to phenylephine in rats is dependent on the vascular bed and the age of the animal.
